destination.title: De Sitter compactifications: construction, obstruction and control
destination.question: Under which source-specific ingredients and approximations can compactifications produce de Sitter solutions, stabilize their fields and withstand consistency, stability and control checks?
destination.summary: The original proposal supplies numerical membership without a written scientific scope. Its membership is useful as a heterogeneous family, including comparative gravity models and supergravity methods. A flux-only, four-dimensional, metastable-only or Swampland-only interpretation would lose supported material. The overview below is a new scoped proposal, not an independently agreed replacement.

systems: Type IIA and IIB compactifications, including geometric and generalized flux models
targets: Existence of de Sitter critical points and metastable minima
Moduli stabilization, scalar stability and vacuum persistence
Finite and parametric control, quantization and scale separation
Obstructions, landscape structure and conditional phenomenological applications
regimes: Finite parameter values and asymptotic families, assessed separately
Retained-sector stability and fuller scalar spectra, assessed separately
assumptions: Ingredients, source content and truncations remain local to each source
A stationary point does not by itself establish metastability or a controlled string background
A necessary condition is not a sufficient existence or stability criterion
conventions: External dimension and parent spacetime dimension are distinct
Graph relations describe source objects and are not automatically physical premises
Source-scoped singletons do not establish cross-source uniqueness
includes: The higher-dimensional, type IIB control and perturbative D-term probes
excludes: Treating numerical membership as scientific equivalence
Treating all de Sitter critical points as minima
Treating asymptotic exclusions as exclusions of every finitely controlled vacuum
Absorbing black-hole reconstruction or QCD applications into the compactification core

sources.title: Lifetime of Stringy de Sitter Vacua

evidence.text: Can fluxless M-theory stabilization by a racetrack and hidden meson yield a de Sitter vacuum with a sufficiently broad geometric decompactification barrier?

sources.title: Moduli stabilization, large-volume dS minimum without D3-bar branes, (non-)supersymmetric black hole attractors and two-parameter Swiss cheese Calabi-Yau's

evidence.text: Can flux stabilization admit finitely separated vacua for identical fluxes, and can nonperturbative corrections produce a large-volume nonsupersymmetric de Sitter minimum without an anti-D3 uplift?

sources.title: WEAKLY-coupled IIA Flux Compactifications

evidence.text: Can restricted-flux type-IIA Calabi–Yau compactifications reproduce LARGE-volume phenomenology through exponentially weak coupling, controlled moduli stabilization and a tunable de Sitter uplift?

sources.title: Complete classification of Minkowski vacua in generalised flux models

evidence.text: Which generalized-flux models in the isotropic type II orientifold class admit nonsupersymmetric Minkowski extrema with all retained moduli stabilized, and can stable extrema be continuously deformed to de Sitter?

sources.title: The Flux-Scaling Scenario: De Sitter Uplift and Axion Inflation

evidence.text: Can flux-scaling AdS constructions be extended to stable Minkowski or metastable de Sitter vacua using positive brane-tension or flux-induced D-term contributions, and can the resulting models support axion monodromy inflation with the required scale hierarchy?

sources.title: de Sitter Extrema and the Swampland

evidence.text: Can a classical positive-potential stationary point provide a string-theory counterexample to the de Sitter gradient conjecture after flux quantization, source consistency, and correction control are imposed?

sources.title: de Sitter Extrema and the Swampland

evidence.text: Do the de Sitter extrema survive resolution of orbifold singularities and inclusion of the new moduli and fluxes carried by the resolved cycles?

sources.title: A dS obstruction and its phenomenological consequences

evidence.text: Can abelian flux stabilize a positive runaway potential into controlled lower-dimensional de Sitter solutions, and what restrictions follow if such solutions are forbidden in quantum gravity?

sources.title: Moduli Stabilization with Non‐Geometric Fluxes — Comments on Tadpole Contributions and de‐Sitter Vacua

evidence.text: Can H,F,Q,R,F3 compactifications yield a consistent, controlled and fully stable de Sitter vacuum, and can the proposed tadpole-sign restriction be derived from first principles?

sources.title: Self-mirror Large Volume Scenario with de Sitter

evidence.text: Can self-mirror compactification reconcile large volume with a T-dual/mirror description and generate de Sitter vacua through nonperturbative Kähler-modulus contributions?

sources.title: On (A)dS solutions from Scherk-Schwarz orbifolds

evidence.text: Can curvature, quantized fluxes and supersymmetry-breaking one-loop Casimir energy produce controlled, metastable de Sitter vacua in type II Scherk-Schwarz compactifications? What distinguishes the corresponding anti-de Sitter solutions?

sources.title: An M-theory dS maximum from Casimir energies on Riemann-flat manifolds

evidence.text: Can calculable Casimir energy and quantized flux on smooth, nonsupersymmetric Riemann-flat manifolds support controlled de Sitter critical points without singular sources?

sources.title: De Sitter vacua in string theory

evidence.text: Can warped type IIB flux compactifications stabilize all moduli, then admit controlled supersymmetry breaking that produces metastable de Sitter vacua? Can their lifetimes exceed cosmological times while remaining below the de Sitter recurrence time?

sources.title: de Sitter string vacua from perturbative Kahler corrections and consistent D-terms

evidence.text: Can perturbative Kähler stabilization of the volume modulus be combined with a gauge-consistent D-term uplift to obtain metastable de Sitter vacua in type IIB flux compactifications?

sources.title: Lifetime of Stringy de Sitter Vacua

evidence.text: Preserve the axion isometry during stabilization, gauge it with magnetic D7 flux, and use the positive D-term for uplift. The isometry is an input condition, so the construction cannot be transferred unchanged to a shift-breaking superpotential.

sources.title: Moduli stabilization, large-volume dS minimum without D3-bar branes, (non-)supersymmetric black hole attractors and two-parameter Swiss cheese Calabi-Yau's

evidence.text: Complex-structure stabilization solves covariant superpotential equations, including τ=(fᵀΠ̄)/(hᵀΠ̄). Kähler stabilization uses the N=1 scalar potential with perturbative and nonperturbative α′ corrections and theta-function-dressed Euclidean D3 instanton contributions.

sources.title: WEAKLY-coupled IIA Flux Compactifications

evidence.text: Orientifold-truncate N=2 prepotential data to obtain N=1 K and W, solve the dilaton/Kähler F-terms, and analyze the scalar potential. The appendix matches these equations to the mirror IIB ISD condition G₃=−i⋆G₃, including the corrected prepotential.

sources.title: Complete classification of Minkowski vacua in generalised flux models

evidence.text: At V=0, write the potential as an exponential prefactor times a quadratic polynomial in x=(ReS,ReT,ImS,ImT). Analytically eliminate these fields using x0=−M⁻¹m, leaving the reduced function V_red=m0−mᵀM⁻¹m and equations V_red=∂ReZ V_red=∂ImZ V_red=0.

sources.title: The Flux-Scaling Scenario: De Sitter Uplift and Axion Inflation

evidence.text: The numerical inflation treatment re-solves heavy-field extremum conditions as the axion varies and evaluates single-field slow-roll quantities with the induced kinetic metric. The pivot is chosen to match the quoted spectral index; the reported scalar amplitude is used to infer Hinf.

sources.title: de Sitter Extrema and the Swampland

evidence.text: Integrating the source equations removes delta functions and yields tractable necessary equations. The resulting de Sitter extrema require a separate localization test; the paper supplies no general existence theorem for intersecting-source solutions.

sources.title: LVS de Sitter vacua are probably in the swampland

evidence.text: Do corrections omitted from the standard LARGE-volume effective potential remain small enough to establish the existence, vacuum energy and stability of candidate de Sitter vacua?

sources.title: Compactifying de Sitter space naturally selects a small cosmological constant

evidence.text: Does compactifying a positive-cosmological-constant higher-dimensional theory on multiple dynamical flux-supported spheres produce a distribution of lower-dimensional de Sitter vacua that accumulates at zero cosmological constant?

sources.title: On SUSY-breaking moduli spaces of AdS$_{7}$ vacua and 6D SCFTs

evidence.text: Does the apparent flat direction suggested by an earlier scan survive an analytic treatment at fixed quantized flux and source content? Singular boundary conditions complicated numerical error control and identification of the sources in the proposed deformed solutions.

sources.title: De-Sitter vacua via consistent D-terms

evidence.text: Can gauge-consistent D-terms produce locally stable de-Sitter or Minkowski vacua with spontaneously broken N=1 supersymmetry and no residual scalar flat directions, with possible applications to flux compactifications?

sources.title: Constructing stable de Sitter in M-theory from higher curvature corrections

evidence.text: Can higher-curvature corrections and G7 flux lift the sole volume flat direction of geometric, non-supersymmetric Minkowski compactifications to produce metastable de Sitter vacua at large volume?

sources.title: New constraints on classical de Sitter: flirting with the swampland

evidence.text: Can the classical de Sitter branch 0 < λ < 1 be excluded using curvature positivity, three stationarity conditions and the F3 Bianchi identity alone, or are additional flux equations essential?

sources.title: Weakly Coupled de Sitter Vacua with Fluxes and the Swampland

evidence.text: Can classical type IIA fluxes and localized sources stabilize the universal volume and inverse string coupling in a parametrically controlled de Sitter regime? The displayed potential supplies the common setting for the explicit no-go arguments.

sources.title: Testing Swampland Conjectures with Machine Learning

evidence.text: How do energies and scalar masses of isotropic type IIB flux vacua populate regions relevant to de Sitter and AdS conjectures? The retained fields are the complex-structure, axio-dilaton, and Kähler moduli, with non-geometric fluxes contributing to stabilization.

sources.title: Membrane instantons and de Sitter vacua

evidence.text: Can membrane-instanton corrections to the universal hypermultiplet geometry, combined with type IIA background flux, stabilize the hypermultiplet moduli in a metastable de Sitter vacuum?

sources.title: Beginners lectures on flux compactifications and related Swampland topics

evidence.text: How do flux compactifications stabilize moduli and determine the sign and size of vacuum energy? Can they yield parametrically controlled metastable de Sitter or AdS vacua with decoupled massive towers?

sources.title: On the distribution of stable de Sitter vacua

evidence.text: How can stationary points of generalized-flux compactifications be parameterized systematically, and where do isotropically stable de Sitter regions occur within their parameter space?

sources.title: Systematic exploration of the non-geometric flux landscape

evidence.text: Can axionic flux polynomials enable systematic analytic exclusion of fully stabilized Minkowski and de Sitter vacua in an isotropic non-geometric flux model, and which configurations remain unresolved?

sources.title: $T$ -dualizing de Sitter no-go scenarios

evidence.text: Which type IIB de Sitter and slow-roll obstructions follow by T-dualizing known type IIA flux no-go scenarios, and how do Bianchi-identity restrictions and factorized moduli geometries determine when those obstructions persist?

sources.title: Metastable de Sitter vacua in N=2 to N=1 truncated supergravity

evidence.text: When can a consistent N=2 to N=1 truncation remove the instabilities of a parent de Sitter vacuum, and what restrictions on scalar geometry and inherited gauging permit metastability?

sources.title: Searching for slow-roll moduli inflation in massive type IIA supergravity with metric fluxes

evidence.text: Can geometric fluxes permit slow-roll moduli inflation or de Sitter extrema in massive IIA compactifications, and which restrictions on moduli dependence and allowed fluxes obstruct them?

sources.title: Membrane and fivebrane instantons and 0 geometry

evidence.text: How do wrapped membrane and NS fivebrane instantons correct the universal hypermultiplet geometry in type IIA compactifications, and can membrane corrections contribute to moduli stabilization and metastable de Sitter vacua after flux gauging?

sources.title: Rigid nongeometric orientifolds and the swampland

evidence.text: How are flux, axion, localized, and D-term contributions assembled before testing IIA de Sitter restrictions? Appendix B imports a generic two-derivative N=1 potential, rather than constructing a controlled vacuum in this window.

sources.title: On the limitations of non-geometric fluxes to realize dS vacua

evidence.text: Which conditions on moduli and generalized fluxes exclude de Sitter extrema in type IIA compactifications, and how much further can these exclusions be classified under an F-term alignment Ansatz?

sources.title: On classical de Sitter solutions and parametric control

evidence.text: Can specific type IIB de Sitter compactifications satisfy flux, source and lattice quantization together with classical string control, and can a scaling improve control parametrically or evade proposed asymptotic de Sitter obstructions?

sources.title: Bounds on Slow Roll at the Boundary of the Landscape

evidence.text: Can Type IIA examples with intermediate εV and ηV satisfy a finite-distance descent bound even when familiar local criteria appear strained? The tested model has fourteen real scalars and four imported flux choices.

sources.title: On de Sitter vacua in type IIA orientifold compactifications

evidence.text: Can perturbative and membrane-instanton corrections inherited from the N=2 universal hypermultiplet provide an intrinsic uplift from AdS to metastable de Sitter after orientifolding a type IIA compactification on a rigid Calabi–Yau threefold?

sources.title: Warped de Sitter compactifications

evidence.text: Under what metric and matter-field conditions do warped higher-dimensional solutions contain de Sitter spacetime, and can internal flux stabilize the compact-space scale in a lower-dimensional cosmological model?

sources.title: Testing Swampland Conjectures with Machine Learning

evidence.text: Can random-matrix typicality explain the observed vacuum exclusions? The paper proposes a probabilistic origin for refined de Sitter and AdS scale restrictions within its selected flux model, motivated partly by earlier random-potential and entropic arguments.

sources.title: Systematics of Type IIA moduli stabilisation

evidence.text: Can a unified treatment of classical type IIA flux potentials systematically classify extrema, their supersymmetry and perturbative stability, and the restrictions on de Sitter solutions and AdS scale separation?

sources.title: Is there a string theory landscape?

evidence.text: Do proposed flux compactifications establish a discretuum of quantum-gravity models, particularly metastable de Sitter states, and could observational or anthropic selection make that discretuum predictive?

sources.title: Asymptotic Flux Compactifications and the Swampland

evidence.text: Can asymptotic Hodge theory classify large-field flux potentials and determine whether constraints on de Sitter vacua, controlled AdS sequences and axion backreaction extend beyond weak coupling and large volume?

sources.title: On Issues in Swiss Cheese Compactifications

evidence.text: Can corrected Swiss-cheese compactifications support a nonsupersymmetric de Sitter minimum without anti-D3 uplift and axionic slow-roll inflation? Separately, how can extremal black-hole charges and fake superpotentials be obtained from prescribed attractor moduli?

sources.title: de Sitter in non-supersymmetric string theories: no-go theorems and brane-worlds

evidence.text: Can a ten-dimensional dilaton–form-field theory admit de Sitter or Minkowski external vacua after compactification on a closed internal manifold with localized sources and internal warping?

sources.title: On the Cosmology of Type IIA Compactifications on SU(3)-structure Manifolds

evidence.text: Can geometric flux permit de Sitter vacua or closed-string slow-roll inflation in type IIA SU(3)-structure compactifications, particularly the explicitly studied coset models?

sources.title: Weakly Coupled de Sitter Vacua with Fluxes and the Swampland

evidence.text: Can flux compactifications support de Sitter minima while a control parameter improves without bound? The paper separates this asymptotic question from the existence of individual vacua at finite large volume and weak coupling.

sources.title: Quadratic curvature corrections to stringy effective actions and the absence of de Sitter vacua

evidence.text: Do dilaton-coupled Gauss–Bonnet corrections weaken or strengthen the Montero–van Riet–Venken (MvRV) obstruction to de Sitter flux compactifications?

sources.title: Large Volume Scenario from Schoen Manifold with de Sitter under Swampland Conjecture

evidence.text: Can self-mirror Schoen compactifications support large-volume de Sitter vacua through nonperturbative effects when the Euler-characteristic-dependent correction vanishes, while satisfying the quoted asymptotic swampland bound?

sources.title: On classical de Sitter solutions in higher dimensions

evidence.text: Which classical type-II orientifold compactifications to D>4 can satisfy necessary existence and perturbative-stability conditions for de Sitter vacua, as tested by the universal volume and dilaton directions?

sources.title: Rigid nongeometric orientifolds and the swampland

evidence.text: Can different consistent flux choices evade existing de Sitter restrictions or produce new ones when all displayed axion dependence is retained? Appendix B identifies this application but supplies no resulting inequality or controlled vacuum within this window.

sources.title: Inflationary Constraints on Type IIA String Theory

evidence.text: Can controlled type IIA Calabi–Yau compactifications support inflation or de Sitter vacua, and which additional ingredients can evade an obstruction derived from volume and dilaton scaling?

sources.title: Issues in type IIA uplifting

evidence.text: Can a positive F-term sector uplift stabilized AdS vacua of a simplified massive type IIA flux compactification to metastable de Sitter vacua with positive cosmological constant?

sources.title: Fully stable dS vacua from generalised fluxes

evidence.text: Can generalised fluxes produce de Sitter extrema with positive masses in all 14 real, including non-isotropic, scalar directions of an N=1 STU model, and how are nearby stable regions organised?

sources.title: de Sitter-eating O-planes in supercritical string theory

evidence.text: Can large spacetime dimension D parametrically control α′ and localized-source backreaction corrections in proposed supercritical de Sitter flux compactifications?

sources.title: O'KKLT at finite temperature

evidence.text: Can thermal corrections or reheating remove the finite-volume de Sitter vacuum of an uplifted compactification? The paper compares one-exponential and racetrack superpotentials and asks which vacuum a cooling system can approach.

destination.title: De Sitter constructions, obstructions and effective control
destination.question: Under which source-specific assumptions can string/M-theory backgrounds or excited states exhibit de Sitter geometry, and what establishes their consistency, stability and effective description?
destination.summary: A proposed navigation family spanning classical and quantum constructions, vacuum and excited-state interpretations, and related reduction and cosmology questions. Neither numerical proximity nor shared de Sitter terminology establishes scientific equivalence.

systems: Type II, heterotic and bosonic string settings
regimes: Classical analyses with their stated correction exclusions
assumptions: Higher-dimensional solutions, lower-dimensional extrema and controlled string configurations are separate tests.
conventions: De Sitter metric or isometries do not by themselves establish a stable vacuum.
Excited states and vacua remain distinct.
Dimensions are retained where supplied, not defaulted universally to four.
Graph relations describe source objects and do not automatically impose question premises.

Adjacent action, reduction and cosmological applications with explicit alternate homes

Identification of common overview membership with fine-question equivalence

sources.title: Quantum Corrections and the de Sitter Swampland Conjecture

evidence.text: Can higher-dimensional string or M-theory equations realize de Sitter behavior while satisfying a potential-gradient conjecture, and can the same configuration admit a controlled four-dimensional effective field theory?

sources.title: de Sitter vacua in the string landscape

evidence.text: Can quantum corrections to a time-dependent compactification be organized into an effective expansion, and how does that organization change with internal-volume evolution, flux time dependence and torus dependence?

sources.title: de Sitter Vacua in the String Landscape: La Petite Version

evidence.text: Determine whether static or evolving internal compactification data can support quantum-corrected de Sitter equations together with a controlled lower-dimensional expansion. Solving the equations and establishing a Wilsonian effective action remain distinct issues in the source.

sources.title: de Sitter Vacua in the String Landscape: La Petite Version

evidence.text: How can evolving internal fields be integrated out to obtain a Wilsonian action, and do the resulting de Sitter configurations represent vacua or coherent states over supersymmetric solitonic minima?

sources.title: de Sitter Space as a Glauber-Sudarshan State: II

evidence.text: Can a controlled four-dimensional de Sitter EFT in type IIB be realized as a Glauber-Sudarshan state across different slicings, and what temporal dependences of fluxes and couplings does consistency require?

sources.title: Almost classical de Sitter?

evidence.text: Can leading four-derivative corrections to localized O-plane/D-brane actions support metastable de Sitter vacua while bulk string corrections and higher source corrections remain negligible, especially in CDT1, CDT2 and specified variants?

sources.title: Transient de Sitter and Quasi de Sitter States in SO(32) and E$_8$ x E$_8$ Heterotic String Theories

evidence.text: Can four-dimensional transient de Sitter and quasi-de Sitter excited states be constructed in SO(32) and E8 × E8 heterotic theories while satisfying quantum equations of motion, Bianchi identities, flux quantization and anomaly cancellation under explicit time dependence?

sources.title: TASI Lectures on de Sitter Vacua

evidence.text: How can quantized fluxes, quantum corrections and warped supersymmetry breaking produce stabilized four-dimensional candidate de Sitter vacua, and how can errors in the approximate effective theory be assessed?

sources.title: Realisation of de Sitter space as an excited state in string theory

evidence.text: Can the type IIB construction of four-dimensional de Sitter space as a Glauber–Sudarshan excited state be extended to heterotic SO(32) and E8 × E8 theories, with controlled EFT evolution and compatible axion constraints?

sources.title: Quantum Corrections and the de Sitter Swampland Conjecture

evidence.text: Specify the kinetic metric, compute the directional derivative, apply the dual-norm inequality, and divide by the displacement norm. This transfers a premise rather than generating a universal positive constant.

sources.title: de Sitter vacua in the string landscape

evidence.text: Project each sector of the target-minus-soliton metric onto solitonic modes and use those coefficients in a coherent-state exponential. Background fluxes must be supplied simultaneously; they are not automatically generated by the metric state.

sources.title: de Sitter Vacua in the String Landscape: La Petite Version

evidence.text: Move to a dual description with an action, organize correction operators by field and derivative content, and compare their scaling with the field equations. Here this operation is applied to an M-theory uplift of type IIB de Sitter compactifications.

sources.title: de Sitter Space as a Glauber-Sudarshan State: II

evidence.text: Treat wrapped instantons and nonlocal counterterms through trans-series and nested internal integrals. The authors argue for finite local contributions after integration/resummation, conditional on suppression or decoupling of sufficiently high orders of nonlocality.

sources.title: Almost classical de Sitter?

evidence.text: Dimensional reduction in the smeared approximation gives Einstein-frame scalar potentials. Scaling in selected dilaton/volume combinations yields on-shell relations between vacuum energy and diagonal Hessian entries; a negative diagonal entry implies a tachyon by Sylvester's criterion.

sources.title: Transient de Sitter and Quasi de Sitter States in SO(32) and E$_8$ x E$_8$ Heterotic String Theories

evidence.text: Use Chern–Weil transgression, ∂t X8 = dΘ7, to distinguish local time dependence from integrated characteristic data. The integral is constant on smooth closed eight-manifolds; the construction attributes surviving time variation to effective orbifold boundaries.

sources.title: de Sitter vacua in the string landscape

evidence.text: Can evolving internal geometry and fluxes support IIB four-dimensional de Sitter isometries with constant Newton's constant? The paper studies this through an M-theory uplift and quantum-correction hierarchies.

sources.title: What if string theory has a de Sitter excited state?

evidence.text: Can four-dimensional de Sitter arise as an excited state over a supersymmetric Minkowski vacuum, avoiding the authors' objections to vacuum constructions while satisfying quantum equations of motion and effective field theory criteria?

sources.title: de Sitter vacua in the string landscape

evidence.text: Can time-dependent compactification geometry, fluxes and quantum corrections support four-dimensional de Sitter isometries with constant Newton coupling and a controlled effective field theory, despite obstructions found for time-independent internal configurations?

sources.title: One-loop bosonic string and De Sitter space

evidence.text: What one-loop two-derivative effective action follows from bosonic-string massless amplitudes, and can its extrapolation beyond the critical dimension admit de Sitter solutions at weak coupling and small curvature?

sources.title: A novel construction of de Sitter vacua in heterotic string theory

evidence.text: Can non-geometric heterotic R-flux, a torsionful O(α′) correction and hidden-sector nonperturbative dilaton dynamics produce a controlled, metastable four-dimensional de Sitter subsector?

sources.title: A Computational Companion to Transient de Sitter and Quasi de Sitter States in SO(32) and E<sub>8</sub>× E<sub>8</sub>Heterotic String Theories I: Formalisms

evidence.text: Can transient four-dimensional de Sitter geometry arise as a metric expectation value in an excited string/M-theory state, with controlled EFT evolution and acceptable axionic couplings?

sources.title: de Sitter vacua in the string landscape

evidence.text: Can evolving internal shape and fluxes restore quantum control while keeping the effective gravitational coefficient constant? The paper compares constant-volume and varying-volume branches with a fixed type IIB coupling.

sources.title: Quantum Corrections and the de Sitter Swampland Conjecture

evidence.text: Can quantum-corrected flux compactifications support four-dimensional de Sitter geometry while retaining a controlled supergravity description? The supplied analysis studies this through an M-theory background related to type IIB by dimensional reduction and T-duality.

sources.title: Quantum Corrections and the de Sitter Swampland Conjecture

evidence.text: Which fluxes and quantum corrections can support an assumed type IIB de Sitter metric, and can those ingredients remain time independent?

sources.title: Constraining de Sitter Space in String Theory

evidence.text: Can classical heterotic string theory realize maximally symmetric de Sitter vacua once all world-sheet effects, including high-curvature physics, are included? Which assumptions or omitted quantum effects could evade a world-sheet obstruction?

sources.title: de Sitter Excited State in Heterotic E8×E8${\rm E}_8 \times {\rm E}_8$ Theory

evidence.text: Can dynamical Horava-Witten walls yield a weakly coupled heterotic E8×E8 transient de Sitter excited state respecting four-dimensional NEC, and support an axion with a time-dependent decay constant in the stated cosmological range?

sources.title: Tachyonic de Sitter Solutions of 10d Type II Supergravities

evidence.text: Might a mildly unstable de Sitter stationary point coexist with a classically controlled string realization, as suggested by an analogy with scale-separated AdS constructions?

sources.title: How a four-dimensional de Sitter solution remains outside the swampland

evidence.text: Can internal time dependence and quantum corrections support four-dimensional type-IIB de Sitter solutions with an effective field theory, and why does the corresponding time-independent ansatz fail?

sources.title: de Sitter State in Heterotic String Theory

evidence.text: Can four-dimensional de Sitter geometry exist in SO(32) heterotic string theory as a finite-domain Glauber–Sudarshan excited state over a supersymmetric Minkowski background, despite the vacuum obstructions discussed by the authors?

sources.title: dS Spaces and Brane Worlds in Exotic String Theories

evidence.text: Can a Lorentzian-string orientifold retain wrong-sign closed fields that evade a de Sitter no-go argument while supporting an ordinary four-dimensional gauge coefficient?

sources.title: On the de Sitter swampland criterion

evidence.text: Do unstable ten-dimensional de Sitter solutions violate a conjecture about four-dimensional quantum-gravity effective theories? The paper separates three possibilities: invalid backgrounds, a mismatch between consistent and low-energy truncations, and a weaker criterion concerning stable vacua.

sources.title: Resurgence of a de Sitter Glauber-Sudarshan State: Nodal Diagrams and Borel Resummation

evidence.text: Represent the specified warped de Sitter target as an excitation of a static soliton while retaining time-dependent supporting fields.

sources.title: Automated consistent truncations and stability of flux compactifications

evidence.text: Can left-invariant scalar reductions with orientifolds and D-branes be automated, their consistency established, and their spectra used to assess perturbative stability of known de Sitter, Minkowski and anti-de Sitter backgrounds?

sources.title: Four-Dimensional Null Energy Condition as a Swampland Conjecture

evidence.text: The construction asks which external FLRW histories can be supported by time-dependent internal geometry and fluxes while retaining a constant four-dimensional Newton coupling and an organized M-theory effective action.

sources.title: Classical de Sitter Solutions of 10-Dimensional Supergravity

evidence.text: Can massive type IIA supergravity admit four-dimensional de Sitter compactifications obtained directly from the full ten-dimensional equations with localized, backreacted orientifolds, and how far can weak coupling and small curvature justify their classical description?

sources.title: de Sitter Vacua in the String Landscape: La Petite Version

evidence.text: Can a type IIB compactification with an external de Sitter metric retain an effective description when its internal warp factors and fluxes evolve, while the axion, type IIB dilaton and four-dimensional Newton constant remain fixed?

sources.title: A new de Sitter solution with a weakly warped deformed conifold

evidence.text: Does the displaced four-dimensional de Sitter extremum admit a ten-dimensional construction including flux quantization, the anti-D3-brane, quantum corrections, and gaugino condensation?

sources.title: Resurgence of a de Sitter Glauber-Sudarshan State: Nodal Diagrams and Borel Resummation

evidence.text: Can a time-dependent geometry arise as an excited-state expectation value while heavy modes are defined on a static supersymmetric reference vacuum?

sources.title: de Sitter vacua in the string landscape

evidence.text: Can a coherent state over an AdS type IIB soliton produce de Sitter geometry? The source leaves this open because localized excitations alter the compactification as well as spacetime, while static internal profiles resist the stated on-shell construction.

sources.title: Open problems on classical de Sitter solutions

evidence.text: Can classical type II supergravity with Op/Dp sources support four-dimensional de Sitter spacetime? The paper fixes a commonly used smeared compactification ansatz to formulate existence, stability, and string-control questions.

sources.title: Moduli Stabilization with Non‐Geometric Fluxes — Comments on Tadpole Contributions and de‐Sitter Vacua

evidence.text: Can classical fluxes stabilize every closed-string scalar in a type IIB Calabi–Yau O3/O7 orientifold, and can the resulting four-dimensional theory admit a consistent stable de Sitter vacuum?

sources.title: de Sitter Vacua in Type IIB String Theory: Classical Solutions and Quantum Corrections

evidence.text: Can ten-dimensional type IIB compactifications with fluxes and localized sources yield four-dimensional de Sitter geometry, and what conditions must quantum curvature corrections satisfy to evade classical obstructions?

destinations.title: Can higher-dimensional string or M-theory equations realize de Sitter behavior while satisfying a potential-gradient conjecture, and can the same configuration admit a controlled four-dimensional effective field theory?

Can quantum corrections to a time-dependent compactification be organized into an effective expansion, and how does that organization change with internal-volume evolution, flux time dependence and torus dependence?

Determine whether static or evolving internal compactification data can support quantum-corrected de Sitter equations together with a controlled lower-dimensional expansion. Solving the equations and establishing a Wilsonian effective action remain distinct issues in the source.
How can evolving internal fields be integrated out to obtain a Wilsonian action, and do the resulting de Sitter configurations represent vacua or coherent states over supersymmetric solitonic minima?

destination.title: Brane backreaction, stability and flux geometry
destination.question: How do brane sources, fluxes and gravitational backreaction affect admissible geometries, metastability and effective dynamics in the supplied settings?
destination.summary: No original scientific region statement was supplied beyond candidate numerical membership. That membership is usable as a navigation proposal: antibranes in flux throats form a coherent core, while several sources address different observables or systems. The overview branches below preserve those differences without interpreting co-membership as physical equivalence.

systems: Antibranes in KS, CGLP and other specified flux backgrounds
Localized-source compactifications and warped brane probes
Conifold throats, brane junctions and exotic branes as neighboring settings
targets: Backreaction admissibility, metastability, polarization and decay
Thermal horizon diagnostics and flux-throat phases
Effective dynamics, holographic infrared structure and conditional vacuum tests
regimes: Probe, perturbative, nonlinear, matched and effective descriptions remain distinct
Extremal and finite-temperature questions remain distinct
assumptions: A local configuration is not automatically a stabilized compact vacuum
Conjectural vacuum tests retain their separate stated premises
conventions: Expected source self-energy is distinguished from additional flux singularities
Charge orientation, asymptotics and comparison roles remain source-specific
includes: Alternative interpretations and historically qualified assertions
Useful alternate homes outside the narrower antibrane core
excludes: A universal conclusion about antibrane metastability or de Sitter uplift
Equivalence inferred solely from shared methods, branes or horizons
Promotion of source-object relations into independently verified premises

sources.title: Polchinski-Strassler does not uplift Klebanov-Strassler

evidence.text: Can the three-form singularity of backreacted anti-D3 branes in Klebanov–Strassler be avoided by regular boundary conditions or resolved by D5 polarization, and what does this imply for antibrane uplifting?

sources.title: Tachyonic Anti-M2 Branes

evidence.text: Does anti-M2 backreaction necessarily produce singular magnetic flux in CGLP, can M5 polarization resolve it, and what do the resulting polarization potentials imply for localized anti-M2 interactions?

sources.title: Localised Anti-Branes in Flux Backgrounds

evidence.text: Can localized anti-brane flux singularities be hidden behind regular finite-temperature horizons, and does their extremal flux structure support a polarization resolution and metastable expanded-brane states?

sources.title: Observations on fluxes near anti-branes

evidence.text: Can necessary IR–UV gluing conditions permit polarized anti-D3 configurations whose three-form divergence is ordinary NS5 self-energy, and can polarization relax an assumption behind finite-temperature singular-horizon no-go arguments?

sources.title: From black holes to flux throats

evidence.text: How do topology, flux and Smarr relations connect nonsupersymmetric flux throats with black-hole constructions, and can NS5 polarization make anti-D3 backreaction compatible with an acceptable source singularity?

sources.title: Polarised antibranes from Smarr relations

evidence.text: What does a background-subtracted Smarr relation require for regular backreacted anti-M2 configurations in CGLP, distinguishing smearing, localization, M5 polarization, extremality and finite temperature?

sources.title: An effective theory for higher-dimensional black holes and applications to metastable antibranes

evidence.text: Can blackfold theory support the existence of polarised antibrane equilibria beyond DBI probe arguments, determine the KPV state's classical stability, and describe thermal transitions of the KP state?

sources.title: On matched asymptotic expansions of backreacting metastable anti-branes

evidence.text: Can a regular leading-order matched asymptotic supergravity solution be constructed for polarized anti-D3 charge on spherical NS5-branes, providing direct evidence beyond the necessary blackfold constraint equations?

sources.title: Brane / flux annihilation and the string dual of a nonsupersymmetric field theory

evidence.text: Can anti-D3 branes in the Klebanov–Strassler throat produce a metastable nonsupersymmetric vacuum, how does it decay through brane/flux annihilation, and what gauge-theory vacuum could describe it holographically?

sources.title: Polchinski-Strassler does not uplift Klebanov-Strassler

evidence.text: Computes a probe D5 DBI-plus-Wess–Zumino potential with n dissolved anti-D3 units. A large-n expansion produces quadratic, cubic and quartic radial terms, whose coefficient inequality is used to exclude finite-radius extrema.

sources.title: Tachyonic Anti-M2 Branes

evidence.text: Reduce the symmetric supergravity ansatz to a one-dimensional system with six radial functions and two superpotential choices. Introduce conjugate ξ modes and use their first-order equations and infrared Taylor expansions to constrain regular solutions.

sources.title: Localised Anti-Branes in Flux Backgrounds

evidence.text: Solve the extremal perturbation equations analytically and classify their near-throat modes. The paper checks numerics against analytic β=0 hypergeometric solutions and reports vanishing horizon energy flux Tab k^a k^b.

sources.title: Observations on fluxes near anti-branes

evidence.text: Compare local metric/dilaton scaling and flux-leg orientations using e⁻φ|H3|² = e^(φ−8A−2f)|αF3+X3|². Evaluate horizon potentials and charges to obtain MADM = Vol4(αH Q3 + bH Q5 Vol2), then combine this with the polarized-cycle volume and anti-D3 mass scaling.

sources.title: From black holes to flux throats

evidence.text: Match the expected asymptotic anti-D3 ADM mass to near-source flux behavior through the Smarr relation. This constrains backreaction without solving all local equations of motion.

sources.title: Polarised antibranes from Smarr relations

evidence.text: A Noether/Komar construction, with dimensional reduction along brane spatial directions, extends the ADM energy prescription beyond asymptotically flat transverse spaces. A counterterm with ξ = d log H subtracts CGLP energy; supergravity equations move the energy surface integral from infinity to the horizon.

sources.title: Perturbative anti-brane potentials in heterotic M-theory

evidence.text: What perturbative four-dimensional bosonic effective action, anti-brane potential and gauge thresholds follow from heterotic M-theory when brane and anti-brane backreaction is included?

sources.title: Anti-D3 Branes: Singular to the bitter end

evidence.text: Can the fully nonlinear backreaction of anti-D3 branes smeared over the deformed-conifold tip connect negative D3 charge in the infrared to KS positive-flux charge in the ultraviolet without additional singular three-form energy densities?

sources.title: Resolving anti-brane singularities through time-dependence

evidence.text: Can singular fluxes near anti-branes be interpreted as the stationary description of an instability, resolved by time-dependent flux attraction followed by brane-flux annihilation? The intended application is anti-D3 metastability in the Klebanov–Strassler throat.

sources.title: Brane-Antibrane Backreaction in Axion Monodromy Inflation

evidence.text: Does direct five-brane backreaction invalidate the localization and warping assumptions of axion monodromy models containing an NS5/anti-NS5 pair on distant homologous two-cycles? The paper approaches this through a calculable D5/anti-D5 interaction potential.

sources.title: Unstoppable brane-flux decay of $ \overline{\mathrm{D}6} $ branes

evidence.text: Does backreaction destroy probe-level metastability of anti-D6 branes against brane-flux annihilation, even when the antibrane-to-flux ratio p/M is arbitrarily small?

sources.title: Mass-deformed M2 branes in Stenzel space

evidence.text: Construct finite-temperature, internally symmetric CGLP black branes and investigate their thermodynamics, possible topology changes, and ability to support negative horizon M2 charge as a regulator of smeared anti-brane singularities.

sources.title: Remarks on brane and antibrane dynamics

evidence.text: How should brane self-field divergences be treated beyond the probe approximation, and does a properly matched brane EFT imply instability or metastability for a single antibrane in a flux background?

sources.title: Backreaction of Localised Sources in String Compactifications

evidence.text: When does smearing preserve physical compactification solutions and low-energy observables? Can localised-source boundary data determine the cosmological constant and diagnose anti-brane flux singularities?

sources.title: Classical de Sitter solutions in three dimensions without tachyons?

evidence.text: Do anti-branes possess stable positions once their forces from orientifolds, fluxes, and possible warped regions are included?

sources.title: Localised anti-branes in non-compact throats at zero and finite $T$

evidence.text: Can finite-temperature horizons cloak the singular three-form energy densities sourced by localized anti-branes in non-compact warped throats, particularly anti-D3-branes in KT and KS?

sources.title: Tachyonic de Sitter Solutions of 10d Type II Supergravities

evidence.text: Can adding anti-branes alter scalar instabilities while retaining a complete higher-dimensional solution?

sources.title: Assessing a candidate IIA dual to metastable supersymmetry-breaking

evidence.text: Can symmetry-preserving linearized deformations of the CGLP background describe backreacting anti-D2 branes and furnish a candidate dual to metastable supersymmetry breaking without additional unacceptable IR flux singularities?

sources.title: Klebanov-Strassler black hole

evidence.text: Can genuine Klebanov–Strassler black holes with spontaneous chiral symmetry breaking be constructed, what thermal phases do they represent, and can their horizon D3 charge satisfy the proposed test for shielding an anti-D3 singularity?

sources.title: Loop corrections to the antibrane potential

evidence.text: Does the inter-brane potential for localized anti-D3 branes at the Klebanov-Strassler tip develop a gap or a repelling tachyon when backreaction is small but finite, after perturbative corrections?

sources.title: On the Existence of Meta-stable Vacua in Klebanov-Strassler

evidence.text: Do anti-D3 branes at the bottom of Klebanov-Strassler source a backreaction compatible with a metastable vacuum of the same supersymmetric field theory, or do their infrared boundary conditions require ultraviolet deformations of the theory?

sources.title: Bifid Throats for Axion Monodromy Inflation

evidence.text: Can an explicit local geometry and holographic gauge theory realize the bifid throat needed for five-brane axion monodromy, including homologous infrared two-cycles and a quantitative treatment of five-brane-pair backreaction with warping?

sources.title: Giant Tachyons in the Landscape

evidence.text: Does five-brane polarization resolve the infrared pathology of localized, backreacting anti-D3 branes at the Klebanov–Strassler tip into metastable states, or do NS5 and oblique channels reveal an instability relevant to de Sitter uplift?

sources.title: Throat destabilization (for profit and for fun)

evidence.text: Do the disappearance thresholds of Klebanov–Strassler black holes and antibrane-supported KS configurations have the same dependence on string coupling and conifold flux when their energies above extremality are expressed in common units?

sources.title: Classical de Sitter solutions in three dimensions without tachyons?

evidence.text: Can a compact G2 throat redshift anti-D2 energy while retaining a polarization barrier against brane-flux annihilation?

sources.title: Brane polarization is no cure for tachyons

evidence.text: Can polarization into five-branes stabilize D3/anti-D3 configurations with a brane-brane-repelling tachyon, once nonspherical shell perturbations are allowed?

sources.title: Perturbative decay of anti-branes in flux backgrounds due to space time instabilities

evidence.text: Can spatial clumping of screened anti-brane charge create an energetically downhill NS5 configuration path from the KPV state to the true vacuum, even when the homogeneous configuration has a tunneling barrier?

sources.title: Fatal attraction: more on decaying anti-branes

evidence.text: Does antibrane backreaction enhance brane-flux annihilation enough to remove the KPV metastable state, and can antibranes consequently provide controlled supersymmetry breaking and uplift? The paper focuses on the local flux accumulation rather than requiring a large disturbance of the throat's UV geometry.

sources.title: Cosmological Constant, Near Brane Behavior and Singularities

evidence.text: Can the classical cosmological constant be determined from localized-source boundary data without solving the full bulk geometry, and can this constrain singularities produced by localized anti-D3-branes in a compact Klebanov–Strassler throat?

sources.title: Supersymmetry Breaking Warped Throats and the Weak Gravity Conjecture

evidence.text: Does a DSB sector that is consistent in isolation remain stable inside the near-horizon geometry of many regular branes?

sources.title: Brane/flux annihilation in double-throat system

evidence.text: How does brane/flux annihilation change flux distributions and relative geometry in two homologically related throats, and under what endpoint conditions does it restore their equivalence?
